s: Identity the person who received Nandampudi Village as a grant from Rajaraja Narendra
x:
Rajaraja Narendra, the celebrated Eastern Chalukya ruler, granted the village of Nandampudi to Nannayya Bhattu, the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature. The grant is recorded in the famous Nandampudi Inscription, which also provides valuable information regarding Nannayya's literary achievements and his role in translating the Mahabharata into Telugu. The inscription remains one of the most important sources for the literary history of Andhra.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which of the following Chalukya-Chola Viceroys had assumed the title Sarvalokasraya, Sri Vishnuvardhana and celebrated his coronation at Jananathapura (Draksharama)?
x: Raja Raja Chola Ganga, who served as the Chalukya-Chola Viceroy of Vengi, assumed the traditional Eastern Chalukya titles Sarvalokasraya and Sri Vishnuvardhana, thereby asserting continuity with the earlier Eastern Chalukya rulers. He celebrated his coronation at Jananathapura (present-day Draksharama), an important political and religious centre of the Vengi kingdom. The remaining rulers listed did not assume these specific titles or celebrate their coronation at Jananathapura.
n: Raja Raja Chola Ganga – Chalukya-Chola Viceroy

Which of the following statements is/are incorrect?
I. Saktivarma had married Kundavai, the daughter of Raja Raja Chola I.
II. Raja Raja Narendra had married Ammangaidevi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola I.
III. Rajendra Chalukya had married Madurantaki, the daughter of Rajendra Chola II
x:
The Eastern Chalukyas maintained close matrimonial relations with the Imperial Cholas, which helped strengthen political alliances between the two dynasties.
Statement I: Incorrect. Saktivarma I did not marry Kundavai, the daughter of Raja Raja Chola I. It was Vimaladitya, the younger brother and successor of Saktivarma I, who married Kundavai, daughter of Raja Raja Chola I. This marriage laid the foundation for close Chola–Eastern Chalukya relations. Statement II: Correct. Raja Raja Narendra married Ammangaidevi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola I. Their son was Rajendra Chalukya, who later became the famous Kulottunga I, founder of the Chalukya-Chola line. Statement III: Incorrect. Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) married Madhurantaki, but she was the daughter of Rajendra Chola I, not Rajendra Chola II.
Therefore, this statement is incorrect.
Hence, Statements I and III are incorrect.
n: Vimaladitya married Kundavai (daughter of Raja Raja Chola I)
Raja Raja Narendra married Ammangaidevi (daughter of Rajendra Chola I)
Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) was born from this alliance and later established the Chalukya-Chola dynasty.

s: The king who is said to have developed Kandukur on the model of Bezawada was
x:
Vijayaditya II of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty is credited with developing Kandukuru into a prosperous town comparable to Bejawada (Vijayawada). His reign witnessed the expansion of temples, trade centres and urban settlements in the Vengi region.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Vijayaditya II developed Kandukuru like Bejawada.

s: Who of the following rulers built Rajahmundry?
x:
Rajaraja Narendra is traditionally credited with the development and construction of Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) as an important capital of the Eastern Chalukyas. His reign is remembered as the golden age of Telugu literature because he patronized Nannaya, the Adikavi of Telugu.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who among the following carried out a naval invasion of Southeast Asia?
x:
Rajendra Chola I launched a famous naval expedition to Southeast Asia around 1025 CE. His powerful navy defeated the Srivijaya Empire, which controlled important maritime trade routes across the Malay Peninsula and Indonesian islands. The expedition demonstrated the naval strength of the Cholas and helped establish their influence over international trade in the Indian Ocean.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Which Chola king defeated the Sailendra king by sending a naval expedition to the Srivijaya Empire?
x:
Rajendra Chola-I launched a remarkable naval expedition against the Srivijaya Empire in Southeast Asia around 1025 CE. His navy defeated the Sailendra rulers, bringing important maritime trade routes under Chola influence. This expedition demonstrated the naval strength of the Cholas and greatly enhanced India's maritime prestige.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Naval expedition to Srivijaya → Rajendra Chola-I
